newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa sees 1997/98 sugar crop 2.3 to 2.4 mln T.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa sees 1997/98 sugar crop 2.3 to 2.4 mln T.

text.p: South Africa's new 1997/1998 sugar crop could be between 2.3 million and 2.4 million tonnes after good rains in the sugar producing areas, the South African Cane Growers' Association said on Wednesday.
The 1997/1998 crop estimate was provisional, the association's chief economist Brian Sugden told Reuters.

"The first estimate has come in at just over 22 million tonnes of cane and that should convert to somewhere between 2.3 and 2.4 million tonnes of sugar. But that is a very early provisional estimate," Sugden said.
Sugden said the final estimate for the 1996/97 crop (April-March) was 2.27 million tonnes.
He said the new season was marked by good follow-up rains in the sugar producing areas of KwaZulu-Natal province.
"We obviously had good follow-up rains, some of the mills have opened. It is early days yet, off course lots of things can happen between that and achieving the 2.3 or 2.4," Sugden said.
A crop of between 2.3 and 2.4 million tonnes of sugar would leave just over a million tonnes of sugar for export.

South Africa produced only 1.67 million tonnes of sugar in the 1995/96 season and last season was the first good crop after five years of drought which cost the industry millions of rands in lost revenue.
